rule: `hint` and `description` are for a new developer who is not very technical and does not know the code base. Say what the class or connection is FOR and where it fits; never how the code works. Do not restate code, signatures, types or algorithms, and explain any jargon in a few plain words. Implementation detail belongs in code comments, or in `review` / `rules` for their own purposes.

hint.what: One short plain line (about 80 characters) shown on the box or line: what it is for.
hint.who: A new developer who is not very technical and does not know this code base.
hint.not: How the code works: no types, function names, signatures or algorithms; no unexplained jargon.
hint.good: Sends chat messages between players; everything that talks to the server goes through it
hint.bad: Uses a Dictionary<int, Peer> and calls rpc_id() per message

description.what: A few plain sentences: what the class (or connection) is for, what uses it, and what a newcomer should watch out for.
description.who: A new developer who is not very technical and does not know this code base or what the class is for.
description.not: A walk through the code: no restating of functions, types or algorithms (that belongs in code comments); no problems (use review).
description.good: Keeps the list of items in a shop and their prices. The checkout and the shelf display both read from it. Changing a price here changes it everywhere at once.
description.bad: Holds a List<Item> and sorts it with a comparer in Refresh(); GetPrice() returns item.price * taxRate.

review.what: Findings from a code review: smells, risks, suggested splits with concrete targets.
review.who: Developers about to change or clean up this code.
review.not: What the class is for (hint/description) or do-nots (rules); no praise or plain description.
review.good: 3800 lines; move the chat functions into a separate ChatLog class

rules.what: Things never to do here, one rule per line; shown to anyone (and any AI) changing this code.
rules.who: Anyone, human or AI, about to edit this code.
rules.not: Descriptions, wishes or findings; only firm do-nots, each with its reason if it is not obvious.
rules.good: Never call the Server from here; go through the Chat system

status.what: stable / wip / fragile / deprecated: how safe it is to change.
status.who: Anyone deciding how carefully to touch this code.
status.not: Anything else: reasons go in review or rules.

tags.what: Short free labels for search and grouping, comma separated.
tags.who: Anyone searching or filtering the map.
tags.not: Sentences, or the class's own name; no duplicates of status or domain.
tags.bad: this is the thing that plays sounds

level.what: How high up it shows: 1 is the top picture, higher numbers are more detail.
level.who: Anyone reading the map from the top down.
level.not: How important the class is; it is how much detail you need before it appears.

domain.what: The broad area it belongs to, in one or two plain words.
domain.who: A newcomer scanning the map for an area.
domain.not: A code folder or namespace; a sentence; a new name when an existing domain fits.
